## 1. How much power will you need?

These are planning estimates for 48 hours, assuming no air conditioning, electric heating, or other large appliances.

| Fridge type | Typical fridge use/day | Suggested battery for weekend |
|---|---:|---|
| Propane absorption fridge (running on propane) | ~70–290Wh for controls, depending on model | 1,000–1,500Wh |
| 12V compressor fridge | ~400–660Wh | 1,500–2,000Wh |
| Residential 120V fridge | ~1,200–1,500Wh | 3,000–4,000Wh |
| Absorption fridge running on electricity | ~2,400–4,700Wh | Not practical with a small station |

Allow another 100–200Wh daily for LED lights, charging phones, and small incidental loads. Add 15–20% for losses and reserve. Actual consumption varies with temperature and your RV's equipment. <Cite refs={["turn373287view0"]}/>
